subject: REL
course_description: Examination of major social, ethical, and theological issues confronting post-Vatican II Catholicism, including the intellectual and historical roots of contemporary debates.
course_notes: This course satisfies the Religion major requirement:- Tradition-Christianity. This course explores the diverse and complex realities of contemporary Catholicism, a global religious tradition with roughly 1.3 billion (official) members. Guided by the assumption that ¿identity¿ is a central question of modern Catholic thought, this course will explore a range of theological, political, and cultural debates about Catholicism¿s defining features, its standards of belonging, and its role in contemporary life. The course will survey the modern history of the Catholic Church from the 16th century to the present, then connect that history to present-day conversations around ecology, technology, social justice, gender, and race. The course will explore these questions by engaging with official church documents, theological texts, art, literature, film, internet culture, and ritual.
